case_studies.title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI
case_studies.abstract: Routing to select large language models (LLMs) with different cost-quality trade-offs has become a fundamental deployment feature of enterprise AI. Existing routers, primarily make independent routing decisions for each LLM call. However, agentic applications execute as long-horizon workflows whose quality is determined only by a delayed, task-level outcome. This mismatch prevents per-call routers from correctly attributing feedback to individual routing decisions. Towards mitigating this, we present TRACE-Router, a task-level routing framework that aligns routing with the unit of supervision.
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient routing in AI systems by building a task-level routing framework called TRACE-Router, which aligns routing decisions with the overall task outcome, resulting in improved quality and cost-effectiveness. The framework allows for adaptive online routing for agentic AI applications. This research focuses on AI application optimization, not directly related to general cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper introduces a novel solution for routing to large language models, which directly affects how IT engineers and DevOps teams work on enterprise AI deployments. They propose a task-level routing framework that aligns routing with the unit of supervision, addressing a key mismatch in existing routers. This is highly relevant to IT engineers who manage and optimize LLM APIs, MLOps, and agentic systems. The value within 90 days lies in implementing or proposing a similar solution to clients, improving the routing efficiency of agentic applications.

case_studies.title: MMOE: Modernizing Diffusion Transformers with Efficient Expert Design
case_studies.abstract: Modern large language models scale successfully by pairing capacity growth with efficiency, keeping per-token and deployment costs under control as capacity grows. AIGC Foundation Models (AFMs), especially diffusion-transformer backbones, have begun to adopt sparse experts, but recent efforts mostly enlarge total parameter counts and sparsity ratios without importing the efficiency mechanisms that made LLM scaling practical, so generation quality is seldom balanced against training and deployment cost. case_studies.summary: This research aims to improve the efficiency of large language models by introducing a new architecture design, allowing for better scaling and cost control. The researchers built a modernized diffusion transformer model with efficient expert design, resulting in improved generation quality while keeping costs under control. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving language model architecture and efficiency, rather than cloud infrastructure management or deployment.

It is unlikely that IT engineers will build something, automate something, or flag a risk within 90 days using the knowledge from this paper. case_studies.title: Nanbeige4.2-3B: Unlocking Agentic Capabilities in a Compact Model
case_studies.abstract: We present Nanbeige4.2-3B, a compact general agentic model with 3B non-embedding parameters. It delivers strong performance across code-agent, office-agent, and complex tool-use tasks while maintaining highly competitive reasoning capabilities in mathematics, coding, and science. Nanbeige4.2-3B is pretrained from scratch on 28T tokens with a Looped Transformer that reuses the layer stack to increase capacity without adding parameters. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of creating a compact general agentic model that can perform various tasks, by building Nanbeige4.2-3B, a model with 3B non-embedding parameters that delivers strong performance across multiple tasks. The result is a model that maintains competitive reasoning capabilities in mathematics, coding, and science. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.score_reasoning: While novel as a compact agentic model, the relevance to IT infrastructure and deployment is limited. case_studies.title: Are You Still the Agent I Authorized? Earned Authority under a Fixed Ceiling for Evolving Agents
case_studies.abstract: Long-lived AI agents increasingly evolve after deployment by retaining experience, acquiring skills and tools, revising workflows, delegating work, and moving across task phases. This improves adaptation but creates a distinct authorization problem. Tool-enabled agents can turn model errors and prompt injections into consequential external actions; when evolution occurs under a live grant, the subject exercising that authority or the context in which it acts may no longer match what the user evaluated. Evolution can change both the effects reachable under an old grant and the authority require
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of authorization in evolving AI agents, where the agents' capabilities and actions may change over time, potentially exceeding their original authorized scope. The authors built a framework to address this issue, resulting in a more secure and controlled environment for AI agents. This research affects IT work related to AI and machine learning deployments.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI or machine learning deployments, here is what to do: review your current authorization protocols, assess the potential risks of evolving agents, and consider implementing a framework to ensure earned authority under a fixed ceiling. This flags a risk: if your org uses AI agents that learn and evolve over time, check your authorization controls immediately to prevent potential security breaches. If you do not use AI or machine learning, this research is not directly applicable to your IT infrastructure work.
case_studies.score_reasoning: This paper reveals surprising aspects about evolving AI agents, particularly the authorization problem that arises when agents' capabilities and context change after deployment. While not directly related to IT infrastructure as used in the UK, it touches upon the impact of agentic systems on authorization, making it somewhat relevant to IT engineers working on endpoint management, SSO, and security. IT engineers couldn't use this to build something directly in 90 days but could use this as a concept to discuss with clients or flag as a potential risk in their environments, considering emerging trends in AI deployment.

It aims to solve the problem of creating effective agentic AI systems by understanding every layer of the pipeline. The result is a detailed reference for practitioners building these systems.

case_studies.title: Dynamic Capability Scoping for Enterprise AI Agents: A Synthetic Dataset and Three-Source Permission Architecture
case_studies.abstract: Enterprise AI agents are typically granted static credential sets at configuration time, holding every tool the role might need for every task they perform. This persistent over-privilege expands the attack surface. We argue that capability scoping must follow a dynamic least-privilege principle and be treated as a prevention mechanism before a detection one. A credential that does not exist in an agent's context cannot be misused regardless of the agent's reasoning or evasion sophistication. We outline a three-source architecture instantiating this principle: role-based ceilings, a task-conte
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of over-privileged AI agents by introducing a dynamic capability scoping approach, which was built into a three-source permission architecture, resulting in a more secure and least-privilege access control system. The architecture ensures that AI agents only have the necessary permissions for their current task, reducing the attack surface. This can help prevent AI agent misuse and data breaches.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure with AI agents, here is what to do: review your current permission settings, implement role-based ceilings, and integrate task-context aware permissions to follow the dynamic least-privilege principle. This flags a risk: if your org uses static credential sets for AI agents, check for over-privilege immediately. Implementing this approach can help reduce the attack surface and prevent data breaches.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty score: 12, proposed a new way to scope capabilities in enterprise AI agents. IT Relevance: 12, directly affects the security and deployment of AI agents in enterprise environments.

case_studies.title: LLM-Assisted Ontology Engineering and Construction of a French Legal Knowledge Graph
case_studies.abstract: Maintenance regulations are complex legal texts that are difficult to exploit when addressing a specific case and challenging to integrate into operational systems. This paper presents a two-stage LLM-assisted workflow for French maintenance regulations: ontology engineering from a SEMLEG-based core ontology, followed by construction of an ontology-grounded French legal knowledge graph. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of complex legal text integration into operational systems by building a French legal knowledge graph using a two-stage LLM-assisted workflow, resulting in an ontology-grounded graph. The graph provides a structured representation of maintenance regulations, making it easier to exploit and integrate into systems. This is not directly relevant to general IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data
case_studies.abstract: Pretraining data processing is critical to the downstream performance of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, many existing approaches define a fixed processing strategy at the corpus or domain level and apply it uniformly to many examples, without adapting to the needs of each example. We propose DataOrchestra, a framework that unifies different processing operations and orchestrates an example-specific pipeline for each example. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient pretraining data processing for Large Language Models by building a framework called DataOrchestra, which orchestrates an example-specific pipeline for each example, resulting in improved downstream performance. The researchers created a system that can adapt to the needs of each example, rather than using a fixed strategy. This research may be relevant to IT engineers working with AI and machine learning models.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage Large Language Models, here is what to do: review your current pretraining data processing strategy, consider implementing a flexible framework like DataOrchestra to improve model performance, and assess the potential benefits of example-specific data curation for your organisation.
